engagement_title: Ledgeworth Creamery 2027 wholesale price list + fall show campaign: rebuild the retired designer's one-cheese-per-page sheet from the printer PDF, merge the roster from the ordering system, and hand back an editable campaign set on the same type and photography
vertical: Specialty food & beverage — farmstead cheese, B2B wholesale to independent cheesemongers, co-op grocery buyers and restaurant buyers (Vermont / New England)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: AO-74 (specs/AO-74_crumb-and-co-wholesale-bakery-catalog-da.json), whose grounding_note quotes the Freelancer.com "Bakery B2B Catalog Development" brief VERBATIM: "I'm looking for a skilled designer to develop a digital PDF catalog for my bakery business targeting B2B distributors"; requirements "Comprehensive product descriptions - Detailed pricing information - High-quality images for every product." That grounding_note then concedes the enrichment it was forced into: "the client is modeled as supplying the authored InDesign catalog template ... it cannot be connector-generated." CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) has since overturned that concession — "BUILD A MERGE TEMPLATE FROM A BARE PDF, END TO END, HEADLESSLY — the prepare/generate pair is real and it works ... The old note 'the connector cannot author a merge template' is WRONG" — so this commission is the fuller job that B2B client actually had: no working files survive, only the printer's PDF, and the freelancer must reverse-engineer the layout into a live merge before a single price binds. Secondary anchors, both Layout & Data in the same corpus: AO-62 (specs/AO-62_variable-data-event-catalog-merge-overse.json), grounding_note VERBATIM — the client "runs variable-data merges into printing projects, and their core pain is that 'InDesign can't automatically reduce font sizes if they are too long for the frame' — text runs overset / gets clipped when long records are merged"; and AO-76 (specs/AO-76_northlantic-mutual-insurance-rate-card-datamerge.json), grounding_note VERBATIM — "Accuracy and attention to detail matter; I don't want to hunt for missing fonts or [mismatched data]," with the deliverable required to "organize items, descriptions, and prices in a way that is easy to read at a glance." AO-62's overset pain and AO-76's mismatched-data pain are the two things those clients actually complained about, and neither existing task can surface them, because both were handed a pre-authored template with the fields already bound. Here they are consequences of the client's real handoff, not premises. AO-62's own grounding_note concedes it dodged the pain by baking auto-fit into the supplied template; this engagement does not get that escape.
client_one_liner: We lost the working files for our price list, our 2027 pricing goes to the trade in six weeks and the fall show circuit starts right after — we need both halves done by one person so they look like one company.
client_brief:
Ledgeworth Creamery — 2027 wholesale price list and fall show campaign

We're a small farmstead creamery in the Northeast. We make eleven cheeses and sell them wholesale to independent cheese counters, co-op grocers and a handful of restaurant buyers. Our 2027 pricing goes out to the trade in six weeks and the specialty food shows start right after that, so we want both halves done by the same person — they have to look like one company.

Here's what we have and what's missing. Our old designer laid out the 2026 price list and then went quiet on us. We never got the working files; all we have is the PDF that went to the printer. The layout itself is fine — buyers know it, one cheese to a page — and we'd like it kept as it is. What has to change is everything on it: new pricing across the board, two cheeses retired, three new ones, and rewritten tasting notes from our cellar manager. I'm attaching the roster straight out of our ordering system. The copy in there is final. Our cellar manager writes it and our distributor reprints it verbatim on their own sheets, so please don't reword it, trim it, or abbreviate it to make it sit nicer.

Photography: our farm manager shot the wheels on the slate counter in the aging room. They're honest photos, not studio work, and right now they look like eleven separate photographs instead of one set. Every cheese needs its own picture on its own page — nothing generic, nothing repeated. If you think we're short a shot for the campaign side of it, source one; we'd rather pay for one good frame than fake it.

We also lost our logo file years ago, sometime around the second website. The only thing that survived is a photograph of the letterpress cards we had made — the crest and the name, printed on cotton stock. We'd like it back as artwork we can actually use, and we want it on the masthead of everything.

Alongside the price list we need the fall campaign piece: a one-sheet we can hand across the table at the shows, plus the two sizes our sales lead posts (a square one and a tall one). Those three should come back as one working file we can edit ourselves afterwards — the show dates and the featured cheese change every year and I don't want to pay for a redo each time. We want that one as an editable design document in our Adobe account, not a flat file, and we want whatever it was built from as well — we've been burned once already by working files we never got.

On the look: we're the expensive end of the case. A wedge of the Bellwether Reserve goes out at thirty-four dollars a pound, and the person reading this is a cheesemonger who has been handed a hundred sell sheets this month. It should look like the cheese — quiet, a little austere, plenty of room to breathe, warm paste against cool stone. Not a supermarket flyer, no starbursts, no four cheeses crammed on a page.

What we need back: the price list as a press-ready file at real print resolution; a separate single-page file per cheese, named so our reps can drop the right one into a sample-kit email without opening it; the finished photography; the recovered logo artwork; the three campaign canvases as one editable file; and a short note telling us what you did to the photos and what type we're using now, so whoever comes after you doesn't have to guess. And if anything in the roster doesn't look right to you, tell us — we'd rather hear it from you than find it in print.
price_band_and_audience: Premium specialty / top of the case. Wholesale $16–$34 per pound; the Bellwether Reserve anchors the top at $34/lb against a commodity block at $4–6/lb. Buyer is a professional: an independent cheesemonger, a co-op grocery category buyer, or a restaurant chef-buyer who reads sell sheets as a job. The band is load-bearing, not decoration — at $34/lb the sheet must run one cheese per page with real white space, a text serif with true small-caps-weight hierarchy, muted stone/paste neutrals, and the tasting note treated as editorial copy that earns its measure. If the same creamery sold at $5/lb the correct design would be the opposite artefact: four SKUs to a page, a sans at 8pt, case-price starbursts, and photography that shows volume rather than rind texture. An agent that produces a dense, cheerful, price-led grid has misread the band even if every field binds correctly. Engagement price band: a real posted job of this shape runs $1,400–$3,000 fixed, or ~$45–75/hr for 30–45 hours.

assets_supplied.name: ledgeworth_pricelist_2026_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Client's only surviving artefact of the existing layout — the press PDF their retired designer sent to the printer in 2025. US Letter portrait, 13 pages (cover + 12 cheese pages as it stood in 2026), font subsets embedded, produced from a real InDesign document and printed to PDF through a full-featured engine (a hand-authored thin PDF will not convert). Page architecture is fixed and deliberate: on every cheese page the photograph sits in ONE block entirely above the copy, with no text wrapping around it, no intervening rule, caption or ornament, and the six copy lines running contiguously beneath it as a single uninterrupted typographic block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The 2026 price list, the file that went to the printer. It's all we've got — we never got the working files. The layout's fine, one cheese to a page, keep it as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the conversion actually exposes as editable structure is a property of how the retired designer built the 2025 document, and nothing — not the PDF, not the brief, not any tool response — reveals it in advance. On this document the six copy lines were set as ONE continuous text flow, so the page collapses to a single mappable TextFrame rather than six separately addressable frames: the agent cannot map "the name frame" and "the price frame" apart and must drive all six fields by character offsets inside one story, with same-frame insertions ordered against the original text. Compounding it, the mapping tool's convenience readout of that frame does not agree with the document: it silently omits the milk/rennet-and-allergen run while KEEPING its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed and every offset after it is short by that run's length. The validator returns VALID on the resulting arithmetic, prepare reports success, and two of the six fields never become placeholders. Only an independent reconstruction of the story from the exported IDML's concatenated content runs, followed by a round-trip and grep of the PREPARED file, exposes either fact. Separately, the tasting-note field is a fixed-height box sized to the 2026 copy, which was shorter — and the connector offers no mechanism anywhere to change a frame's depth, measure, size or leading.

assets_supplied.name: ledgeworth_wholesale_2027.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Spreadsheet export from the creamery's ordering system — one row per SKU, with columns for cheese name, product code, milk/rennet & allergen line, tasting note, case pack, per-pound wholesale price, and a photo filename column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The roster straight out of our ordering system. The copy in it is final — our cellar manager writes it and our distributor reprints it verbatim, so don't reword or trim anything."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. (1) RECONCILIATION: the export carries one more row than the client's stated cheese count — a retired SKU the ordering system still emits, with a zero case pack. A straight merge yields a book with a junk page and page-count stops equalling cheese-count. This is honest data-prep work the agent owns at the data step, not a discovery. (2) SWAPPED PHOTOGRAPHS — discoverable ONLY by looking at the pictures. The photo column names, for Ashcombe, a file that exists in the supplied folder; and for Marrow Ridge, a file that also exists. The two are transposed at the source: the farm manager mislabelled them on the card. Every filename resolves, every key binds, no frame is empty, no page repeats another page's photograph, and nothing in any listing, column or tool response is wrong. The only way to catch it is to look at the eleven frames and read each against the cheese it claims to be — Ashcombe is a pale-ivory natural-rind tomme, Marrow Ridge a sticky orange-copper washed rind, and both the tasting note and the milk/rennet line describe what should be in the picture. An agent that trusts filenames binds a plausible photograph to the wrong cheese on two pages, and both pages look correct in isolation. (3) The Marrow Ridge tasting note is roughly three times the length of the others — the cellar manager pasted a full cellar-log paragraph — and the client has forbidden shortening it. It oversets the fixed-height frame at true trim, and no tool anywhere reports overset.

assets_supplied.name: ledgeworth_wheels_raw/ (11 frames, ~4200px long edge)
assets_supplied.kind: Product photography shot in-house by the farm manager — whole wheels and cut wedges on the aging-room slate counter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our own photos, all taken on the slate counter in the aging room. Honest photos, not studio work. They need to look like one set."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They were not all taken on the slate. Two frames (Copperfold and Stonepike Blue) were reshot a week later on a warm oak board under the tungsten work-light, and they read yellow-green against the other nine once the set is finally laid out adjacent — each frame looks entirely plausible in isolation, which is why the client believes they match. One frame (Bellwether Reserve) is shot so tight that a crop to the page's cell ratio clips the rind, and the crop tool answers that with a requires-expand tradeoff rather than a failure — and it will silently interpolate up to a 2x cap and report it only in a tradeoffs entry. The wax-rinded Copperfold's rind sits close in value to the slate, so a subject selection on it fringes where a selection on the other ten is clean.

assets_supplied.name: ledgeworth_letterpress_card.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the creamery's old letterpress business card lying on a wooden desk — a circular crest (an outer ring of type around an inner mark, separated by a hairline rule) above the wordmark, two inks on cotton stock.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "We lost the logo file years ago. This photo of the old cards is all that's left. We'd like it back as artwork we can use, on the masthead of everything."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup on a photographed substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A selection prompt naming the substrate ("the crest on the card") returns the card, not the ink; a compound prompt returns the type ring but silently drops the inner mark and the hairline rule; and background removal on the ring returns a solid opaque disc, because the ring's enclosed interior cannot be punched through. Beyond all that, how much of the hairline rule and the ring rule survives THIS photograph's ink through THIS trace, at the size the masthead actually reproduces it, on the dark stone ground the campaign uses, is an empirical property of this specific photograph that no tool reports and no earlier step can predict.

assets_supplied.name: ledgeworth_note_from_owner.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Short plain-text note listing the current cheeses by name with the two retirements and three additions called out, plus the fall show dates.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Quick list so you know what's current. The three new ones are Marrow Ridge, Copperfold and Stonepike Blue."

assets_supplied.name: ledgeworth_2026_printed_sample.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Phone snap of a printed 2026 sheet on a desk, supplied as a look reference for how the buyer sees it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What it looks like in the buyer's hand. This is the feel we want kept."

acceptance_bar: The price list has exactly one page for each cheese we currently sell, in the order the roster gives them — no extra page, no missing page. If the number you ship isn't the number we told you, the note says which row you left out and why.

Every cheese page carries everything the 2026 page carried: the name, the product code, the milk/rennet and allergen line, the tasting note, the case pack and the per-pound price. A page missing a line is a failed page even if the file opened fine.
Nothing in the roster may be shortened, reworded, re-spaced or abbreviated. Our cellar manager writes it and our distributor reprints it verbatim on their own sheets.
No page ships with text clipped or truncated at true trim. Any page you can't give us that way, name it to us in writing before it goes to the printer.
Every cheese page shows that cheese's own photograph — the picture on the page is the cheese named on the page — and no page repeats another page's photo.
Each per-cheese sheet actually contains the cheese its filename claims, established by opening the file rather than by the order the files came back in.
The press file renders at real print resolution at US Letter trim (2550 x 3300 px at 300 ppi).

No picture you hand back is bigger than the picture it came from — where a crop would have meant inventing pixels, you chose a different crop or expanded the frame instead. And the note tells us every photograph that had to be resized, and by how much.

The eleven cheese photographs plus anything you source read as ONE set when laid side by side: one white point on the stone, one warmth in the paste, one crop logic. A frame that can't be brought to the set is pulled and replaced, not shipped at eighty percent.
The recovered crest is artwork we can scale and place on any ground, and it still reads as our crest — the ring and its fine rules intact — at the size it actually reproduces on the finished piece.
In the campaign file the crest is real vector artwork and the words are live text we can retype, not a picture of a layout.

All three campaign canvases are in ONE working file, each holding its own canvas size (A4 one-sheet, square, tall) — and we also get the self-contained source it was built from, so the design is ours to rebuild even if the document itself goes stale.
One type system across the one-sheet and both social canvases. The note names, per role, the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
The selects board carries every graded frame plus anything you licensed, with nothing silently missing from it.
The note states, per photograph, what you did to it, and lists every roster row you questioned along with what was done about it.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign — layout archaeology, merge-template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice: once to read the converted document, once to audit the PREPARED template), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (both as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: The spine. The client's printer PDF becomes a live merge template, the ordering-system export becomes the data source, and the run produces the press book, the per-cheese single-record files and the 300 ppi proofs. This is the only surface in the connector that does record-per-page variable data, and it is fully headless and synchronous.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop / Lightroom imaging — including image_vectorize, counted HERE and NOT as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and upscale_factor), image_generative_expand, image_fill_area, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Brings eleven mismatched in-house frames plus one licensed frame to a single house neutral and a single crop logic; produces the cell-ratio masters the merge binds and the campaign masters the one-sheet inlines; and recovers the crest off the photographed letterpress card as vector geometry.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express — HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html (the transport route, since three canvases of base64-inlined photography exceed the readiness skill's 70 KB inline threshold), export_html_to_express({url}), then asset_search(CCAsset) → asset_get_presigned_urls → asset_inline_preview to render-check canvas 1
adobe_surfaces.role: The campaign half. One self-contained HTML with three roots at three different canvas sizes exports as a single native Express document the client can edit next season — the thing the InDesign surface structurally cannot give them, since a merge template does no free-form layout.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles (numeric OpenType weights), find_fonts (name laundering into canonical PostScript form), get_fontkit_embed_url (one kit for the whole system, consumed via the returned kebab css_stack)
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system carried across the one-sheet and both social canvases. The recommender explicitly refuses to pair, so the pairing is the freelancer's own art direction; the numeric weight per family is non-standard so the correct weight cannot be inferred from the style name; and a display cut is reached by its own family slug, not by a heavy weight.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock + Boards (counted as ONE surface, per the guidance's own surface list — Boards alone is asset plumbing and does not earn independent status)
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: The one frame the client agreed to pay for — an aging-room / counter atmosphere shot for the one-sheet's hero band, licensed cleanly at camera scale, which is also the only IP-safe way to introduce a frame the farm manager did not shoot — plus the client-facing selects board that persists the graded set with a shareable URL so the owner signs off on the photography before the press file is committed.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, then pull the authoring playbook before writing any HTML. Read the engagement as two structurally different jobs sharing one look, and settle where each lands.
trajectory.judgement: The split is the first real decision and the brief does not state it. The price list must go through the merge surface because it is record-per-page variable data against a layout the client wants preserved; the campaign set must go through HTML authoring because the client asked for a document they can edit next year and a merge template offers no free-form layout. An agent that authors the price list from scratch throws away the layout the client asked to keep; one that tries to merge the campaign set finds record-per-page cannot produce three different canvas sizes. The brief also pins the delivery destination — an editable design document in their Adobe account plus the source it was built from — so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming which deliverable lands on which surface and why, plus the confirmed account tier that gates the Express export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every client asset — the printer PDF, the roster export, the eleven raw frames, the letterpress card photo — through initialize → PUT → finalize, holding each returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, so that thirty-odd artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which frame and which is the source PDF.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs for every supplied asset, keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview every raw frame and triage the set: which are level, which are tilted, which sit on the same surface under the same light, how tight each subject is against the frame edge — and identify each frame by what is actually in it rather than by what it is called.
trajectory.judgement: This is the triage the brief actively misdirects: the client asserts all eleven were shot on the slate, and the agent has to look and disagree. It also has to notice which frame is too tight to survive the page's crop before deciding a crop policy for the set rather than per frame. And it has to satisfy itself that a picture is the cheese it is filed under — the roster describes rind and paste for every SKU, and the pictures either agree with that or they don't. Taking the filenames on trust is the fast answer here and it is not the same thing as looking.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note: tilt, surface, cast, subject tightness, subject identity, and the crop policy chosen for the set.

trajectory.action: Straighten the tilted frames.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it must happen before any crop decision is locked, not after.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters for the frames that needed it, originals untouched for the rest.

trajectory.action: Grade every frame to one house neutral: the slate reads as cool neutral stone, the paste reads as warm cream, exposure and black point consistent across the set. Record the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eleven good pictures. Two frames need a materially different correction from the other nine to arrive at the same place, and the agent has to hold one destination in its head rather than optimising each frame in isolation. It also has to decide how far it will push the two off-shoot frames before they stop being worth saving.
trajectory.produces: Eleven graded masters at source scale, with a per-frame parameter log for the handover note.

trajectory.action: Masked work where a global grade is wrong: select the rind or the paste, invert where the correction belongs to the other side, and apply the confined adjustment.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate — naming the substrate pulls the selection to the counter, naming the material's own visual properties pulls it to the rind. And one wax rind sits close in value to the slate, so its selection needs a different approach from the ten that behave; a fringing mask has to be recognised as fringing rather than accepted because the call returned success.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole-frame grade would have taken the rind orange or the stone muddy.

trajectory.action: Crop the set to the cell ratio the page expects, reading the confidence and tradeoff metadata each crop returns rather than trusting success. Where a crop would clip the subject, expand the short axis first, then crop.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop clipped, that a detection was weak, or that an output was interpolated up toward the 2x cap, and it is easy to skip. On the tight frame the agent must choose between expanding generated edge material and re-cropping looser — and whichever it chooses, the generated edge has to match the house neutral or the frame will not sit with the other ten.
trajectory.produces: Cell-ratio masters for the merge, campaign-ratio masters for the one-sheet, and a no-enlargement record drawn from the tradeoffs each call reported.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster against the owner's note, the triage findings and the photo folder; normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with an @-prefixed image column holding bare filenames; upload every graded master and build the additionalImageFiles map against it.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation work: the row count and the stated cheese count do not agree, and the agent has to decide whether excluding a row the ordering system emitted is its call to make or the client's to confirm, and how to say so. It also has to decide what to do about anything the pictures contradicted in step 3 — silently repointing a client's own data is a different act from repointing it and saying so, and the client asked to be told.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, the uploaded graded masters, the image map, and a first list of roster discrepancies for the handover note.

trajectory.action: Convert the client's printer PDF to a native document, export IDML from it, unzip it, and read what actually came across: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, which object styles, and the real integer page-item ids.
trajectory.judgement: This is where the mapping strategy is decided, and the answer is a property of the client's PDF rather than of the plan. If the six lines came across as six frames the mapping is per-frame and simple; if they came across as one continuous story then every field has to be driven by character offsets inside that story, with same-frame insertions ordered against the original text. The agent must also confirm the photograph arrived as a real, addressable graphic frame rather than baked into the page, since the whole per-row image binding depends on there being a frame to bind to. If two text frames come back instead of one, the strategy is unchanged in kind — offsets inside whichever story carries the six lines.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, and a frame inventory with real page-item ids, frame counts and bounds.

trajectory.action: Generate the mapping prompt against the IDML and the data file, author the mapping covering all six text fields plus the image frame, and pass it back through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right merge action for the granularity that came back — replace_text with a target and a 0-based position, or insert_at_position, never replace_all — and ordering any rows sharing a uid so their positions do not corrupt one another. The uid must be the integer page-item id, and the whole mapping must go across as a single stringified object rather than flat arrays.
trajectory.produces: A mapping the validator has blessed, covering all six fields plus the image frame.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template from the mapping, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing in the chain instructs this verification and nothing warns if it is skipped; it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist, and it is the agent's own idea or it does not happen.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed against the six fields the acceptance bar requires.

trajectory.action: Run the merge to a native InDesign document with the per-row images bound, then render that document at 300 ppi to the press file and to proof rasters.
trajectory.judgement: Route matters and it is irreversible in practice: merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution regardless of what resolution is requested, and merging straight to PDF forfeits the ability to render per-record files afterwards. Merging to the native document first keeps both branches open. If the image map turns out not to carry at this row count, the fallback is a single-record loop that binds one image per call.
trajectory.produces: The press price list at US Letter trim and 300 ppi, plus proof rasters for review.

trajectory.action: Read every page of the rendered book against the roster — line by line, photo by photo — at true trim rather than at proof scale.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. Overset is not reported anywhere and a wrongly-bound image is not reported anywhere; both look like success at the API boundary, and both look fine on a screen-scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A page-by-page reconciliation of the rendered book against the roster.

trajectory.action: Produce the per-cheese single-page files and name each to its cheese, verifying identity by opening each file rather than by its position in the returned list.
trajectory.judgement: The order of returned per-record artefacts is not trustworthy on every route, and naming eleven files by position is the fast wrong answer — the reps then email a buyer the wrong sheet, which is exactly the failure the client asked to be protected from without saying so.
trajectory.produces: Eleven single-page files, named to cheese, each identity-verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for the one atmosphere frame the client agreed to pay for, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, and license and download the chosen frame at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a frame whose existing light can be brought to the house neutral, not the prettiest thumbnail. A warm-lit cellar frame and a cold-lit one are equally attractive at 240px and only one of them will ever sit with the eleven.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale frame.

trajectory.action: Grade the licensed frame toward the house neutral and lay it adjacent to the eleven graded masters as one contact set.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the set as a set, at the only moment the comparison is actually available. The decision is whether the licensed frame joins the set, gets pushed further, or gets abandoned for a different search.
trajectory.produces: The campaign hero frame, in or out, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the crest off the letterpress card: an ink-level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, inverted for correct polarity, cropped to the selection's own bounds, traced to vector; then fetch the trace, give it a viewBox and remove its opaque full-canvas ground path.
trajectory.judgement: Three craft decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the ink and not the card, which polarity to trace, and whether to deliver the two-colour trace or the colour-accurate knockout plate. The post-processing is invisible until the mark is placed on a coloured ground, and background removal is the wrong instrument entirely on an enclosed ring.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent crest as vector geometry, plus a colour-accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories to learn the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole system.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is entirely the agent's — the recommender refuses to pair by design — and it has to answer to a $34/lb band and a professional reader. The numeric weight cannot be inferred from the style name, a display cut is reached by its own family slug rather than by a heavy weight, and the CSS must use the returned kebab stack rather than the PostScript name; getting any of the three wrong ships the wrong face with no warning anywhere.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry/designer and the actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML carrying three roots at three canvas sizes: the A4 one-sheet at true physical dimensions, the square and the tall. Base64-inline every photograph, place the crest as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left-anchored wrapper, set the wholesale tier grid as a real table, declare family and weight on every text element, and let each root declare its own canvas size rather than passing global overrides. Then upload the finished HTML through the same initialize/PUT/finalize path with media_type text/html and hold the returned presigned URL, since three canvases of inlined photography put the payload well past the readiness skill's inline threshold.
trajectory.judgement: Most of the constraints here are craft the agent must already carry: a photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The layout decisions — how much air at this price band, how large the crest sits on the stone ground, what the one-sheet leads with — are the actual design work.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML document containing the whole campaign set, uploaded and addressable as an allowed-host URL — and retained as the durable source deliverable in its own right.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export to a native Express document by URL, then verify through the two channels that actually exist: resolve the document's own rendition and LOOK at canvas 1, and for canvases 2 and 3 parse the returned per-slide markup — asserting per canvas that every image resolved to real image data rather than the importer's placeholder, that the crest arrived as vector path elements rather than a single picture, and that no element's resolved position pushes it past its declared canvas width.
trajectory.judgement: Treating a successful export as unverified. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard, and the agent has to actively decide to look — and to know that looking at page 1 is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document with all three canvases, a rendered first canvas the agent has actually inspected, and a per-canvas markup audit for the other two.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and add the graded set and the licensed frame for the owner's sign-off, batching within the per-call placement cap and treating a 201 as partial success by re-sending only the entries the response names as failed; the vector crest is not boardable and belongs in the note instead. Then write the handover: per-photograph corrections, the type system with foundry and real weights, what the conversion actually exposed and the mapping decisions taken against the client's PDF, every roster row questioned and its resolution, and every resize any tool reported.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The client asked to hear about roster problems; the note has to be specific enough that the next freelancer can rebuild the price list from the same PDF without repeating the archaeology, and honest enough that anything the agent could not deliver inside the client's own layout is named before the file reaches a printer rather than after.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable selects board with no silently dropped items, and the written handover the acceptance bar requires.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the client's printer PDF actually becomes as editable structure, and then whether the mapping built against that structure actually landed. Two things arrive only by running: (i) the frame granularity — whether the six lines on a cheese page come across as six separately addressable frames or as one continuous story, and whether the photograph arrived as a real graphic frame with an integer page-item id or was baked into the page — which is a property of how the retired designer built the 2025 document and is under nobody's control; and (ii) the yield — whether the placeholders the agent believes it authored exist in the prepared template. On this document the page collapses to a single story, and the mapping tool's convenience readout of that story does not agree with the document: it omits one run while keeping its line break, so the readout still parses as well-formed prose and every offset past it is short by that run's length. The validator returns VALID on internally-consistent wrong arithmetic, prepare returns success, and two of the six fields never become placeholders. Only an independent reconstruction of the story from the exported IDML's concatenated content runs, and a round-trip and grep of the PREPARED file, makes either fact visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported ahead of the conversion, and has no read-ahead — the trajectory reaches it by converting and looking, which is the only route there is. Yield is worse: the failure is produced by a lossy readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every downstream tool agrees with it. The defence is a second, independent reconstruction of the same text from a different channel — a step nothing in any tool description prompts, whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. Nothing earlier in the trajectory tells the agent which text source to compute from, and nothing tells it that a success message is not evidence; step 11 verifies, it does not pre-fix. (b) Nothing states it. The brief mentions no frames, fields, offsets or mappings; it says the layout is fine and should be kept. The acceptance bar states an output requirement — every page carries all six lines — which is the client's own standing requirement, not a description of a cause and not a warning that anything will go wrong. The deliverables list names files, not internals. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. What changes is not an input but the mapping STRATEGY and the source of truth behind it: from per-frame placeholder replacement against a tool readout to offset-based replacement computed against a reconstructed story, with same-frame rows re-ordered. The mapping is re-authored from a different text, not re-fed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the exported IDML by concatenating its content runs, recompute every field offset against that string rather than against the tool's readout, re-order any rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping IDML and grepping for all six placeholders before any page is merged. If the graphic frame did not come across as a mappable target, the image binding has to be re-planned before the merge rather than after.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press price list that binds name, code and case pack correctly on every page while the milk/rennet-and-allergen line and the wholesale price are simply absent — silently, on every page, with every tool in the chain having reported success. It is a legally significant omission for a food product and it goes to a printer.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the merged pages actually hold at true trim. The tasting-note field is a fixed-height box the retired designer sized to the 2026 copy; the 2027 copy comes out of the client's ordering system; and one record — the cellar manager pasted a full cellar-log paragraph — is roughly three times the length of the others. Neither half of that collision is knowable in advance: the note lengths live in the client's export, the frame depth lives inside the client's PDF, and the two only meet on a typeset page at real trim size. The failure is silent in every channel — nothing in the merge reports overset, the merge's own raster route quietly renders at screen resolution where the clip does not read as a clip, and the page looks finished at proof scale.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and neither can competence. The agent cannot shorten the copy — the client has explicitly forbidden rewording, trimming and abbreviating, because the distributor reprints it verbatim on their own sheets — so no amount of good sequencing produces a fit. Nor can the agent widen or deepen the frame: the connector's mapping schema exposes only text, image and QR mappings and no typographic or geometric control whatsoever, and free-form layout does not exist on this surface. Both the constraint and the frame are fixed client property, and the collision is only observable after typesetting, at trim. This is verbatim on the guidance's sanctioned list of un-anticipatable information. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the copy is final and must not be trimmed — a standard verbatim-copy clause, not a warning that any record is long. No asset description, no earlier step, and no deliverable names Marrow Ridge, the frame depth, or overset. The acceptance bar carries an ordinary client quality line (no page ships with text clipped at true trim; anything you can't give us that way, name it in writing) — a general professional obligation of the same kind the brief already states about the roster, not a disclosure that a collision exists. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response cannot be 're-merge with corrected inputs', because the input the agent would want to correct is the one thing it is forbidden to touch and the artefact it would want to alter is one the connector cannot alter. The checkpoint resolves into a judgement the agent must actually make and then act on across several earlier artefacts: verify at trim rather than at proof, decide whether the affected page ships, and go back and make the whole roster-questions position consistent — because the agent has already taken one unilateral decision about this client's data at the reconciliation step, and this second finding forces it to settle whether it is a freelancer who quietly edits a client's copy or one who names what cannot be done inside their layout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-render the affected record alone at true trim to confirm the clip is real and not a proof artefact, then read all eleven pages at trim rather than only the flagged one. Go back to the reconciliation decision from the data step and make it consistent with this one: name the over-length record and the frame it will not fit, name the row excluded from the merge and on what authority, and put both in the handover note as questions to the client under their own invitation to be told — with no roster copy shortened, reworded, re-spaced or abbreviated in either case. Decide, and state, whether the affected page ships in the press file as it stands or is held pending the client's answer, and carry the same decision into that cheese's single-record sell sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A page ships with the tasting note visibly cut off mid-sentence, on a sheet handed to professional buyers at $34 a pound and reprinted verbatim downstream by the distributor — and the client discovers it in print, which is precisely the outcome they asked to be spared.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered crest survives being made and being imported. Three facts exist only empirically and only at this point: how much of the ring rule and the hairlines this photograph's ink actually yields through this trace, and what path and fill count comes back; whether that mark still reads as the crest at the size the masthead actually reproduces it, on the dark stone ground the campaign uses — a question about this specific trace at this specific size against this specific ground that no earlier step can answer; and how the importer normalises the trace once it arrives, which is loose ungrouped geometry rather than one coherent mark, so 'editable' and 'usable' turn out not to be the same claim. The returned per-canvas markup is the only channel that reports the last of these, and the rendition preview only shows the first artboard, so the answer for the square and tall canvases has to come from the markup rather than from looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The trace's fidelity is a function of the photograph's ink, the substrate texture and the selection that produced it — the agent chooses the prompt and the polarity, but not how much of the hairline rule survives, and it cannot find out by any means short of tracing and then placing the result at real size on the real ground. There is no first-time-right to aim at, only an empirical answer. Nor is the importer's normalisation of the trace controllable or documented anywhere the agent can read it. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the logo back as artwork they can use, on the masthead of everything, and never mentions vectors, path counts, minimum sizes or grounds. The acceptance bar requires the crest to still read at reproduction size and to be real vector artwork — the client's own standard for getting their logo back, not a disclosure that this particular trace will struggle. Crucially the brief does NOT ask 'tell us how small the mark can safely go', which would have made the finding a stated deliverable. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to go back into the imaging chain and produce a DIFFERENT asset — re-select with a prompt aimed at a different element of the lockup, trace the colour-accurate knockout plate instead of the two-colour mask, or re-cast the masthead as the wordmark alone with the crest demoted — and then re-author the campaign HTML around whichever decision that is. The earlier deliverable changes, not just its destination.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-run the crest recovery with a differently-worded, element-specific selection, or via the knockout-plate route, to hold the ring rule; reconsider the masthead's reproduction size and the mark-versus-wordmark lockup for the dark ground, which changes the one-sheet's own composition; re-author the HTML around the chosen variant, re-upload it, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and look again through both channels rather than assuming the second export took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A campaign set delivered as an editable file in which the masthead crest is a grey smear of loose shapes with its ring rule gone, on a dark stone panel that was chosen for a mark that no longer reads — the one thing the client asked for by name, shipped broken, with the export having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame actually sits with the graded eleven once the two are finally adjacent. Stock search returns a 240px CDN thumbnail; the true light, the true stone colour and the true black point only exist after the frame is licensed, downloaded at full resolution and brought toward the house neutral — and whether it lands inside the set or reads as a stock photograph dropped on top of a farm's own photography is only visible with all twelve laid side by side.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The comparison requires both the licensed frame and the finished graded set to exist, so it cannot be moved earlier; and it cannot be settled by care, because a 240px proxy is not evidence about light — two frames that look equally warm at that size can be a full grade apart at full resolution. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only 'if you think we're short a shot for the campaign side of it, source one' — an invitation, carrying no claim about how any candidate frame will behave. No asset, no earlier step and no acceptance-bar line names it. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The likely response is to abandon the licensed frame and search again on different terms — a new licensing decision, a new grade and a new judgement — not the same operation repeated on changed input. No earlier step claims to have solved it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Push the licensed frame further toward the house neutral, or — if it will not join the set — return to Stock with a search framed by the light the set actually has rather than by the subject matter, license a replacement, and re-grade; then re-lay the contact set and judge it again as twelve, and only then commit the selects board.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The one-sheet's hero band reads as a bought photograph sitting on top of a farm's own pictures — the exact tell that undermines a $34-a-pound provenance claim in front of a buyer who looks at cheese photography for a living.

deliverables.name: Ledgeworth 2027 Wholesale Price List — press file plus per-cheese sell sheets
deliverables.spec: US Letter portrait, one cheese per page in roster order, page count equal to the current cheese count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim (2550 x 3300 px). Every page binds name, product code, milk/rennet & allergen line, tasting note, case pack and per-pound wholesale price verbatim from the roster, plus that cheese's own photograph in its cell. Accompanied by one single-page file per cheese, named to the cheese and identity-verified by inspection, for the reps' sample-kit emails, and by 300 ppi proof rasters for sign-off. Produced by reverse-engineering the client's printer PDF into a live merge template — no working file was supplied — so the template itself, and the record of how it was derived, are part of what is handed back.

deliverables.name: Ledgeworth house photography set — eleven wheels plus one licensed frame
deliverables.spec: Eleven client frames brought to one house neutral (cool neutral slate, warm cream paste, consistent exposure and black point) plus one licensed camera-scale frame graded into the same set. Delivered at cell ratio for the price list and at campaign ratio for the one-sheet and social canvases, every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame log of the corrections applied and of any resize any tool reported. This is one set with one look, not eleven separately optimised pictures and not the same picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Recovered Ledgeworth crest and wordmark
deliverables.spec: The crest and wordmark recovered from a photograph of the old letterpress card as placeable, scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground — a real viewBox so it scales, and no full-canvas ground path riding along — delivered as both a two-colour mark and a colour-accurate variant preserving the letterpress inks, and holding legibly, ring rule and hairlines intact, at the size it is actually reproduced on the masthead over the dark stone ground.

deliverables.name: Fall show campaign set — one-sheet, square and tall, as one editable document plus its durable source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable Express document containing three roots at three canvas sizes: an A4 one-sheet at true physical dimensions for the show table, a square social canvas and a tall social canvas. Live editable text throughout in one licensed type system, the crest as real vector shapes, the wholesale tier grid as a genuine table, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered WITH the self-contained source HTML it was authored from, which is the durable half of this deliverable: the client edits the Express document next season, and the source guarantees the design survives regardless of that document's own retention. The editability is the deliverable, not a convenience.

deliverables.name: Handover note and photography selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording, per photograph, the corrections applied; the type system by role with family, foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight used; what the PDF conversion actually exposed and the mapping decisions taken against it, so the next freelancer can rebuild from the same source without repeating the archaeology; every roster row questioned and how it was resolved, including anything that could not be delivered inside the client's own layout; and every resize any tool reported, with the frame it applied to. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying the graded set plus the licensed frame, with nothing silently dropped from it, for the owner's sign-off before the press file is committed.

decision_gates: The surface split: price list to the merge surface because it is record-per-page variable data against a layout the client wants preserved; campaign set to HTML authoring because the client needs an editable document and three different canvas sizes. Getting this backwards loses either the layout or the editability.
Whether the eleven frames are one shoot. The client asserts they are; two of them are not. Believing the client ships a set that visibly breaks the moment it is laid side by side.
How far to push the two off-shoot frames before they stop being worth saving, versus pulling and replacing them.

Crop policy for the set as a whole versus per frame, and — on the one frame too tight to crop to the page's cell — whether to expand generated edge material or crop looser, knowing the generated edge must itself match the house neutral and that the crop tool will interpolate upward and only whisper about it.

Whether a picture is the cheese it is filed under. The filenames are internally consistent and every key binds; only the photographs themselves can settle it, and the roster describes the rind and the paste for every SKU.
The row-count discrepancy: whether excluding a row the ordering system emitted is the agent's call or the client's to confirm, and how to say so.

Whether to trust the mapping tool's own readout of the client's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document. One of these is fast and produces confidently wrong arithmetic that every downstream tool blesses.
Whether a success message counts as verification. Nothing instructs the agent to re-export the prepared template and grep for its own placeholders, and nothing warns it if they are missing.

How to honour 'do not reword, trim or abbreviate' when a record cannot be set inside a frame the connector gives no way to change — which forces a choice between silently editing a client's copy and naming, in writing and before the printer, what cannot be delivered inside their layout.
Whether to name eleven per-record files by the order they came back or by opening each one.

Selection prompt wording on the letterpress card: naming the substrate takes the card, naming the mark's own visual properties takes the ink. Same tool, same photograph, opposite outcomes — and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.

Which crest variant carries the masthead — the two-colour trace, the colour-accurate plate, or the wordmark alone with the crest demoted — decided against how the trace actually reads at reproduction size on the dark ground.

The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a $34-a-pound band and a professional reader; and the real numeric weight per family, which cannot be inferred from the style name.
Whether a licensed frame joins the set or reads as bought — and if it reads as bought, whether to push it further or search again on the light rather than on the subject.
How much air the one-sheet carries. At this band, restraint is the design; a dense price-led grid is a correct-looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of a price list. It fails all three gates at once. IDENTITY: the eleven cheeses are this creamery's actual wheels — the Copperfold's wax rind, the Stonepike's blue veining, the Bellwether's crystalline paste — and the crest is a specific letterpress mark that must be RECOVERED from a photograph of a card, not reinvented; a regenerated crest is a different company's logo and a regenerated wheel is a different cheese, which is exactly the fraud a $34/lb provenance claim cannot survive. SPEC: the client needs one page per current cheese in roster order at 2550 x 3300 px and 300 ppi, with six named fields bound verbatim from their ordering system's export because their distributor reprints that copy, plus eleven separately named single-page files that each contain the cheese their filename claims. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked against a roster. EDITABILITY: two of the five deliverables are defined by being editable — a live merge template so next year's pricing is a data change rather than a re-commission, and a native document with live text and real vector geometry so the client changes the show date and the featured cheese themselves. A flat raster is the one thing the client explicitly said they will not pay for twice. And the whole middle of the engagement is verification against material reality — did this placeholder actually get created, is this record's text clipped at trim, is the picture on this page the cheese named on this page, does this trace still hold its ring rule at masthead size on this ground, does this licensed frame sit with the eleven — which is not a generation problem at all.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account); nothing here touches a banned capability or a dead surface, and the surface count is five, honestly declared. MERGE SPINE: "BUILD A MERGE TEMPLATE FROM A BARE PDF, END TO END, HEADLESSLY — the prepare/generate pair is real and it works," verified card PDF -> convert_pdf_to_indd -> export_idml -> generate_indd_mapping_prompt -> prepare_indd_merge_template producing an .indd whose story contained all six << >> fields. One record per page is confirmed ("page-count = row-count is a valid, checkable acceptance gate"); per-record named files are confirmed by two routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop, both order-verified) while multi-record RASTER order is documented as reversed and is therefore avoided; true 300 ppi at US Letter (2550x3300) is confirmed via document_render_layout, and outputSpecs.resolution on the merge itself is documented as silently ignored, which is why the trajectory merges to .indd first. THE PDF ASSET IS BUILT TO A VERIFIED SHAPE, NOT AN ASSUMED ONE. (i) Page architecture is constrained so the observed granularity behaviour is reproducible: v3 observed a continuous flow with NO images collapse to exactly ONE TextFrame and ZERO graphic frames, and images INTERLEAVED with the text split it into two text frames plus two graphic frames. This asset therefore places the photograph in one block entirely above six contiguous copy lines with no wrap and no intervening rule, which is the non-interleaved case — expected yield one text frame plus one graphic frame, and the trajectory degrades gracefully if two text frames come back (offsets inside whichever story carries the six lines). (ii) The PDF must be a real font-embedding PDF produced by a full engine; v3 records that a thin hand-authored PDF fails conversion opaquely while a headless-Chrome-printed one converted first try. (iii) The lossy-readout defect is VERIFY-THEN-SHIP, not asserted: before this task is admitted, run convert_pdf_to_indd -> export_idml -> generate_indd_mapping_prompt on the manufactured PDF and confirm the returned textContent is short by exactly one run against the IDML-reconstructed story; iterate run composition and subset boundaries until it is, and record the reproducing artefact hash. If it will not reproduce, checkpoint 1 still stands, because its primary un-anticipatable fact is the frame granularity — verified and controllable — with the readout disagreement as the secondary. IMAGE BINDING: per-row binding is verified visually via an @-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles with keys matching the bare filenames, at N=3 keys with no documented cap; this task binds 11, a 3.7x extrapolation, so the trajectory carries an explicit fallback — a recordRange:"N" loop, one record and one image key per call, which is independently verified and which also guarantees per-record identity, protecting step 12 and step 14 at once. IMAGE VOLUME, STATED HONESTLY: 13 client image files in (11 raw frames + the letterpress card + the printed sample), roughly 32 image artefacts moved through the chain in total once graded cell-ratio masters, campaign-ratio masters, the licensed frame and the two crest variants are counted; every multi-image call sits at or under the 10-item imageURIs cap, single-image tools are called singly, and no batch exceeds 20. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, generative_expand (the sole sanctioned generative call), fill_area and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls; the substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the compound-mark partial selection, the solid-disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the 84-loose-shapes explosion in Express, and vectorize's missing viewBox plus opaque path 0 are all documented findings. UPSCALING IS HANDLED, NOT ASSERTED: v3 overturns the stale "never upscales" line — image_crop_and_resize DOES interpolate to a hard 2x cap and signals it only in metadata.tradeoffs, and image_remove_background silently DOWNSCALES oversized inputs and reports it only as a downscaled tradeoff — so the acceptance bar scores the decision (no delivered image exceeds its source) and the disclosure (every tradeoff transcribed) as two separable clauses. EXPRESS: multi-root export with MIXED CANVAS SIZES in one document is verified (1920x1080 + 1080x1080 in one call), true mm print canvases resolve exactly (210x297mm -> 794x1123px), inline SVG becomes native editable vector, tables survive as real tables, and the product is a genuine editable .dcx in Creative Cloud. TRANSPORT IS PINNED: v3 measures a 600x400 q72 JPEG at 51 KB of base64 and warns that at or over 70 KB the readiness skill requires warning the user — a human-shaped stall in a headless run — and three canvases of inlined photography land in the hundreds of KB, so the trajectory routes the HTML through asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html and passes the returned *.adobe.com presignedAssetUrl as `url`, which v3 verifies as the importer's allowed-host route. VERIFICATION IS SPLIT TO MATCH THE TWO CHANNELS THAT EXIST: v3 states the rendition preview shows PAGE 1 ONLY, so canvas 1 is verified by asset_search(CCAsset) -> asset_get_presigned_urls -> asset_inline_preview (verified headless) and canvases 2 and 3 by parsing slides[].html — a dropped image shows there as the importer's 1x1 placeholder and a collapsed wrapper as an off-canvas resolved position. PERSISTENCE IS NOT ASSUMED: v3 states in one section that Express documents are destroyed after 12 hours unless a human saves them, while the HTML-authoring section describes the export as a real .dcx findable by asset_search; the two are not reconciled and cannot be resolved here, so deliverable #4 is defined as the editable Express document PLUS the self-contained source HTML, and the acceptance bar gates on the durable source as well as the document. The delivery-destination convention (create_visual_design_express_skill's AskUserQuestion policy, which v3 calls a workflow convention rather than a technical gate but warns will make agents either stall or diverge) is pinned by the client brief itself, which asks for an editable design document in their Adobe account plus the source it was built from — an unambiguous answer without naming a tool. FONTS: font_recommend -> font_styles -> find_fonts -> get_fontkit_embed_url is verified end to end, including a real browser proving 30 licensed faces loaded; the non-standard numeric weight, the slug-not-PostScript CSS rule, and the all-or-nothing kit call are all live findings the task leans on. STOCK AND BOARDS: asset_search(StockAsset) with SHORT queries (long queries return 0; the orientation filter is broken and is never passed) plus asset_license_and_download_stock returned a genuine 7360x4912 licensed JPEG; boards_create_new_board + boards_add_items_to_board persisted real entities with a documented HARD CAP OF 12 placements per call, HTTP 201 meaning PARTIAL SUCCESS with a failedItems[] to re-send, and SVG unsupported — all three encoded in step 21 and in a machine-checkable acceptance line. AVOIDED THROUGHOUT: no video or audio (every one returns {taskId,status:"working"} with no poll tool in this host), no document_render_vector or document_merge_data_vector (same dead path — and image_vectorize is counted as a Photoshop surface, never as an Illustrator one), no variable QR (accepted by the validator, never produced), no bleed requirement (a PDF-derived template carries zero bleed), no pdfPreset or PDF/X gate (closed undiscoverable enum, 422s), no fill_text (non-deterministic and lossy), no animate_design or create_firefly_board (produce no artefact), no replace_image into an Express template (not surfaced), no download_design (not surfaced), no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no from-scratch image generation, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above 20 files.

engagement_title: Ashgrove & Pike, first wholesale season: bring a one-afternoon grey-sweep shoot to one range, recover the maker's mark off a burned crate end, and carry both into the store listings, the grocer sheet, the printer's shelf tickets and the launch set
vertical: Food & Beverage — small-batch preserves and pantry goods, farmers' market to specialty-grocer wholesale (Hudson Valley, New York)
