client_one_liner: Make our six jars and the gift crate look like one range on a clean white ground, get our branding-iron mark back off the crate end as artwork we can actually use, and prove both of them on the grocer sheet, the shelf tickets our printer runs, the store page and the launch posts.
client_brief:
Ashgrove & Pike is a preserves kitchen in the Hudson Valley. Marisa and I have cooked six preserves out of a shared commercial kitchen in Kingston for four years and sold them at two farmers' markets and out of the back of the van. This winter we are doing two new things at once: opening a proper store online, and going out to specialty grocers with a wholesale sheet for the spring season.

Both of those need pictures, and ours are not good enough yet. A friend with a good camera came in one afternoon and shot all six jars for us on a roll of grey paper, and the holiday gift crate separately. They look fine one at a time on his laptop and they look wrong next to each other. We need them to read as one range: clean white behind them, square, the jar sitting square in the middle, nothing hanging off the edge, ready to load straight into a store listing. No shadows, no invented reflections, just the jar. We also need versions we can drop straight onto the coloured panel on the grocer sheet, with no white square sitting around them.

The next piece is the one we care about most. Our mark was cut as a branding iron by a man in Rhinebeck who died two winters ago, and it has only ever existed as a burn on the end of a shipping crate. We never had a file and there is nobody to ask. We need it back as proper artwork we can use — on the tickets, on the sheet, on the store page, on whatever comes after — and it has to still be our mark, not a new mark that looks a bit like it.

What we need out of this:
- store pictures for all six preserves and for the gift crate
- versions of the same that can sit straight on colour
- our mark as usable artwork, plus a short note on anything we should know about using it
- a wholesale line sheet for the grocers, A4, with the range set out as a proper list and the prices on it
- shelf tickets, one per preserve, printed from the same artwork our printer ran last spring. We have the file they sent us, not the working file, and nobody here knows how it was put together
- a launch set for the store: a square post, a taller post, and a vertical one for stories
- one wide picture of the whole range on a table for the top of the store page. We do not have one
- a shared reference set that the two of us and our two market managers can all look at, so we brief from the same place instead of four different phones

Everything you hand back has to stay editable by us afterwards. There are two of us and we will be changing prices.

On tone: the jars are 9 to 16 dollars and a case of twelve wholesales at 78. Our customers are 30 to 55, they buy two or three jars at a stall or as a gift, and they read the back label before they buy. It should feel like real food made by people — generous and plain-spoken. Not a 48-dollar luxury conserve, and not a supermarket own-brand either.
price_band_and_audience:
Retail 9 to 16 dollars a jar (Seville marmalade 11, damson and bay conserve 13, sour cherry and black pepper 14, quince paste 12, lemon curd 9, tomato and fennel jam 16 for the large). Gift crate of six at 68. Wholesale case of twelve at 78, keystone to 13-16 on shelf. Audience 30 to 55, Hudson Valley and New York weekenders, farmers'-market and specialty-grocer shoppers who buy two or three jars for themselves or as a gift and who read the ingredient panel before buying.

This band is load-bearing on every design decision in the package. At 9 to 16 dollars the work must read honest-premium: daylight on scrubbed wood, the fruit still looking like fruit rather than lacquered, jars photographed as objects a person handles, a warm paper-neutral ground on the line sheet, type large enough to read across a market table, and prices set plainly inside the run of copy rather than exiled to a discreet column. The failure at this band is a combination, not any one dark surface: a near-black ground plus extreme sparseness plus prices pushed out of the reading line plus food styled into abstraction is the 48-dollar luxury-conserve answer, and it makes a 13-dollar jar look overpriced rather than desirable. A saturated brand-colour panel is a different thing and is correct here — the deep bramble the mark burns to on the crate is the brand's own colour and reversing the mark out of it on the grocer sheet is right, provided the shelf ticket and the store page keep the warm paper ground and the prices stay in the text. Push the same content the other way — bright, busy, a starburst price — and it becomes the 4-dollar supermarket own-brand the client has explicitly ruled out. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes.

assets_supplied.name: sweep_shots/ (6 files)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All six preserves, one afternoon, same roll of grey paper, same spot on the bench. Shot by a friend with a good camera." 5472x3648 each, camera-scale, one SKU per frame: Seville marmalade in clear glass, damson and bay conserve in dark glass, sour cherry and black pepper in a clear clip-top jar, quince paste in a squat clear jar, lemon curd in clear glass, tomato and fennel jam in a large clear jar. Western Latin-script printed paper labels, no people.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The shoot ran past the light. The last two frames of the six — the lemon curd and the quince paste — were made after the bench window went flat and a tungsten work lamp was switched on, so those two carry a different illuminant from the other four. Worse, and only visible once a knockout is actually run: both of those two are pale, near-luminous contents in clear glass sitting at almost exactly the luminance of the grey sweep behind them, so subject detection has no contrast to work with at the glass shoulder. The returned alpha bites into the shoulder on one and leaves a soft grey rim on the other. Nothing in the frames looks wrong on inspection and nothing in the tool response reports it; it appears only as a chewed edge and a grey halo once the cut-out is put on a pure white ground and actually looked at close up. Separately, the sour-cherry jar is the one clip-top in the range and its wire loop stands proud of the lid enclosing a genuine see-through void, which the subject knockout hands back filled with captured grey.

assets_supplied.name: gift_crate_hero.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The holiday gift crate, the thing we most want to sell in December." 5472x3648, the six jars packed in a shallow pine crate on the same grey sweep.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The crate carries a wire bail handle that arcs over the packed jars, and the clip-top sour-cherry jar sits inside it. Between them they enclose three genuine see-through voids that a subject knockout cannot punch: the returned cutout comes back as one opaque blob with all three voids filled with captured grey sweep, which reads as pale slabs of nothing sitting inside the handle arc on the pure white tile. Both calls report full success. The frame also sits about a degree and a half off level, which is not apparent until a square crop is derived from it.

assets_supplied.name: crate_end_mark.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark, burned into the end board of a shipping crate. It is the only version left — the man in Rhinebeck who cut the iron died two winters ago and we never had a file." 4032x3024 phone photograph, shot square-on but hand-held. Dark bramble-brown burn on pale white oak, the Ashgrove & Pike monogram with an ampersand.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The board is open-grain white oak and the iron was held a beat too long on the lower half, so the burn has bled along the grain: fine dark hairs run out of the mark into the wood on the lower third, and the counters of the 'a' bowl and the ampersand's lower eye are partially bridged by bled char. At full canvas the mark looks clean and every trace of it 'succeeds'. The bridged counters and the grain hairs only declare themselves as the mark comes down to the size a real ticket reproduces it, where the hairs read as dirt and the closed counters turn the letterforms into blobs. image_vectorize takes no options at all, so there is no parameter on the tracing step to tune this away — the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be known until the failure is seen.

assets_supplied.name: shelf_ticket_2025_print.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer sent us last spring for the shelf tickets. We do not have the working file and nobody here knows how it was built." A flat press PDF, 90 x 55 mm landscape, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries the preserve name, a tasting line, the origin line, the size line and a price line, a small photograph of the jar, and a small placed mark on a pale panel.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three things nobody at the client could tell you and nothing in the PDF announces. First, the printed card looks like five separately labelled copy fields but the conversion does not expose five frames — the placed images split the flow into TWO text frames, and the split falls in an unobvious place, so some of the five lines share one continuous story and must be replaced by ordered offset arithmetic inside it while the rest sit alone. Second, the two graphic frames come back distinguishable only by their bounds and their link, and the mark's frame is a fraction of the size the printed card suggests — the reproduction size of the recovered mark is geometry inherited from a printer nobody can ask, not a size anyone chose. Third, the mapping readout of the multi-line story silently omits the run holding the origin line while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well-formed and every character offset after it is short by exactly that run's length; the validator returns valid and the placeholder step reports success on offsets that never land.

assets_supplied.name: skus.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our six preserves with the copy that goes on the tickets." Columns for name, tasting line, origin, size, price and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Seven rows for six preserves — the sour cherry is entered twice with two different tasting lines. Headers are mixed-case with trailing spaces, and the photo column is a plain header holding bare filenames that neither match the sweep_shots files as delivered nor satisfy the merge's own image-column contract. And the two rows the client is proudest of carry copy far longer than the rest ('Damson & Bay Leaf Conserve, Small Batch No. 7' and a tasting line that runs to nineteen words), which fits nowhere on a 90 x 55 mm ticket while every other record sits comfortably. On screen at merge time nothing reports it.

assets_supplied.name: market_stall_day.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A picture from the stall, if it is any use to you." A phone frame of the whole range laid out on the market table.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: 1512x2016 — a fraction of camera scale, so it cannot carry the wide store-page hero without interpolation, but it is comfortably larger than a square or portrait launch canvas and therefore a perfectly reasonable candidate for those. It was shot straight into a low autumn sun behind the stall: the whole stall front and the top third of every label are clipped to paper-white with nothing in the highlights to recover. It looks merely 'bright' as a thumbnail and reveals itself as unrescuable only when a highlight recovery is actually applied and moves nothing at all.

assets_supplied.name: house_notes.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: Two paragraphs of colour and tone language from Marisa, with no hex values and no measurements: scrubbed pine, brown butter, orchard shade, bramble, 'warm but never orange', 'the fruit should still look like fruit', 'plain-spoken'.

assets_supplied.name: wholesale_copy.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The grocer-facing copy: case configuration, case price, minimum order, lead time, the paragraph about the kitchen, and the six preserves with their shelf prices.

acceptance_bar: All seven store pictures sit on a pure white ground, square, the product optically centred with nothing touching the edge, and the cut edge holds when inspected close-up — on that white ground, and on the saturated ground for whichever pictures are placed on the coloured panel.

No interpolated pixels anywhere in the delivered package. No delivered file may exceed its source frame's pixel dimensions, and every crop's own tradeoff report must carry no upscale entry. A file that reaches its target size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.

One neutral, one white point and one black point across the six sweep masters, judged with all six adjacent as they will sit in a store listing row rather than one at a time. The cut-out product family and the lifestyle family may sit on two different targets, but each family must agree with itself and the two must not fight when they land on the same page.

The mark is delivered as placeable artwork, not as a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding along underneath it, and it must read as the same mark everywhere it appears in this package, including reversed out of the bramble panel and at whatever size the ticket reproduces it.

Shelf tickets: exactly one page per preserve; every field on every record live in the merged output; every record's full copy actually present on the rendered proof at trim with nothing dropped or truncated, checked on all six and not only on the first; the jar photograph on each ticket the one belonging to that preserve; and the 300 DPI proofs rendered from the merged document rather than requested at merge time.

The collateral is handed over as a native editable document that the two of them can change prices in: every photograph actually visible in it (a grey box is a reject), the mark present as live vector shapes rather than a flattened raster, the line sheet's range set as a real table, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own numeric weight rather than a silent fallback.
The wide store-page frame must sit with the graded set when the two are finally adjacent on the line sheet and the store page — not merely be a good photograph on its own terms.
Every canvas in the launch set must carry a picture that can actually hold at that canvas's size and quality; a canvas is not delivered by being filled.

A written handover: the parameters applied to each frame with one line on why that frame differs from its neighbours, the typefaces chosen and the reasoning for the pairing, and anything we should know about using the mark.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_auto_tone, image_apply_adjustments, image_adjust_single_color_saturation, image_select_by_prompt, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_list_presets, image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize, image_generative_expand, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the engagement lives here and it is the surface the whole commission is judged on. It levels the off-level crate frame before any square crop is derived from it, then fixes ONE product-neutral target from the best-lit sweep frame and corrects each of the six jars toward it with a separate adjustments call per frame, because a single batched call applies one identical parameter set and two of those six were shot under a different lamp. It runs the knockouts and triages their routes: the coherent opaque-content jars go through the one-call knockout onto white, while objects that enclose a see-through void have to be handled as a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled to the white preset, because the direct route cannot punch an enclosed hole. It decides which cutouts can carry a genuine transparent placement onto the grocer sheet's colour and which cannot, since the only alpha source in the family is the same knockout that fills those voids. It recovers the mark at ink level off a photographed burned board by naming the burn's own visual properties rather than the board it sits on, in two raster preparations giving two states of the mark plus a high-resolution plate for the surfaces that cannot take vector, and it does the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not do for you. It runs the single sanctioned generative call to widen the wide frame for the vertical canvas and then has to bring that synthesised band into the house neutral before it is usable. It is also the only place the client's own market-stall frame can actually be assessed, since the question is whether anything is left in its highlights. image_vectorize is counted here, in the Photoshop family where it belongs, and not as an Illustrator surface; the genuine Illustrator tools are deliberately never called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host.

The type system for the line sheet, the store page, the launch set and the mark specification. One recommendation pass per typographic role rather than a pairing request, because the tool refuses to pair by design — so the pairing is entirely the agent's art direction, and it has to land on the 9-to-16-dollar farm-shop band rather than the luxury-conserve one. Numeric OpenType weights are read from the style inventory rather than assumed, because weight mapping is non-standard per family and writing the reflexive value ships the wrong cut with no warning. Every name is laundered through find_fonts into canonical PostScript form before the kit is built, because one unresolvable name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it, and the CSS then has to reference the returned css_stack slug rather than the PostScript name or it falls back silently. Note that no font from this surface can reach the InDesign ticket — there is no font file download — so the ticket's typography is the printer's and the agent's typographic authorship exists only on the Express surface.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: Turns the printer's flat 2025 shelf-ticket PDF back into a live merge template with no working file to start from. Converts it, exports the IDML to read the real frame inventory before promising any field map, reconstructs the true story text from the IDML content runs rather than trusting the mapping readout, builds the mapping against whatever the conversion actually exposed, binds the recovered mark into its graphic frame as a static high-resolution plate and the per-preserve jar photographs into the other graphic frame as a genuine per-row image merge, prepares the template and verifies the placeholders by re-exporting rather than trusting the success message. Then runs the six preserves at one record per page, branches to a press PDF for the printer and to per-record single-page files through the route whose record identity is guaranteed, and renders the 300 DPI client proofs from the merged document rather than asking for resolution at merge time, where it is silently ignored.

adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, export_html_to_express, asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: All the designed collateral as one native editable document at mixed canvas sizes, so the two founders can change prices in it afterwards: the A4 wholesale line sheet with the range as a real editable table and the mark reversed out of the bramble panel, the store page with the wide hero, the mark specification page, the three launch canvases at square, portrait and vertical, and the written handover. Every photograph has to be pulled down and base64-inlined because an image left as a URL renders as an empty grey box at full HTTP success, the mark is inlined as live SVG so it stays editable vector rather than a picture, the font kit is embedded verbatim as the one permitted external stylesheet, everything is anchored from the top left with explicit sizes because right-anchored auto-sized wrappers collapse and throw their contents off the canvas, and the whole payload is uploaded and passed by URL because seven inlined photographs put it far past the inline threshold. The export is verified by parsing the returned HzHTML and by pulling the document's own rendition back and looking at it — which shows page one only, so the page the agent most needs to see has to be page one.

Sources the wide table scene of the range that the client asked for and cannot supply, IP-clean and at genuine camera scale, with generative-tech candidates excluded and with short generic queries because a long descriptive query returns nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero. It is also where the house grade gets tested against something it did not create, since the search thumbnail is a 240-pixel proxy carrying no usable colour information and the frame's real illuminant and ground tone are only visible once it has actually been licensed and downloaded. The Boards half persists the shared reference set the two founders and their two market managers all brief from: the graded masters, the white-ground primaries, raster representations of the recovered mark and the licensed wide frame, placed across more than one call because the cap is twelve placements per call and vector is not accepted, with a partial-success response read as partial rather than as done. It is a real shareable artefact with verifiable entity ids, and the selection of what belongs on it is art direction rather than plumbing.

trajectory.action: Upload every client raster headlessly and actually look at each frame before touching a parameter: the six sweep shots side by side, the crate hero, the burned crate end, and the market stall frame.
trajectory.judgement: Read the set as a set rather than as eight jobs. Recognise that this is two colour problems and not one — the sweep frames are a cut-out product family that wants a neutral product target, while anything lifestyle wants the warm house look from the founders' notes — and log what each frame's dimensions do and do not permit, without yet ruling any frame in or out on quality.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame diagnosis, a dimensional budget for every downstream canvas, and an explicit decision that the product family and the lifestyle family will be corrected to two different targets.

trajectory.action: Level the frames that are off before any crop geometry is derived from them.
trajectory.judgement: Straighten first. A level correction applied after a square crop has been cut invalidates every tile derived from it, and the crate hero's roll is small enough that it will not be noticed until the crop edge exposes it.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters for the crate hero and any rolled sweep frame.

trajectory.action: Fix one product-neutral target from the best-lit sweep frame and correct each of the six jars toward it individually, one adjustments call per frame, logging the parameters as you go.
trajectory.judgement: Not one global move across the batch, and not an auto-tone per frame either — both fracture when all six sit adjacent in a store listing row. The clear-glass jars and the dark-glass conserve need different highlight handling to reach the same neutral, and the fruit must still read as fruit rather than as a corrected colour patch.
trajectory.produces: Six neutral-agreed sweep masters and the first half of the applied-settings log.

trajectory.action: Bring the crate hero to the same product-neutral target as the six.
trajectory.judgement: The crate is a product shot, not a lifestyle shot, even though it looks like a scene. It belongs to the family it will sit beside on the store listing, not to the family it resembles.
trajectory.produces: A neutral-agreed crate master.

trajectory.action: Run the knockout pass — put the jars onto the pure white ground in one call each — and then actually inspect each returned cutout close-up rather than as a whole frame: drive a tight crop off an explicit selection's returned bounding box at the shoulder and preview that crop, because a whole-frame preview is a downscaled proxy in which a few pixels of edge cannot be read.
trajectory.judgement: Use the direct route where the subject is one coherent blob with real contrast against the sweep, and look at every result rather than only the first — the whole point of a set is that it is only as good as its worst frame. The tool exposes no edge, threshold or feathering parameter, so inspection is the only instrument there is.
trajectory.produces: White-ground primaries for the preserves the direct route serves, plus a close-up edge reading on every frame.

trajectory.action: Route the objects the direct knockout will not serve differently: select the grey sweep material by naming it, invert that selection, and fill to the white preset rather than asking for a subject knockout.
trajectory.judgement: Triage rather than repetition. An object that encloses a see-through region hands that region back filled with captured sweep from the direct route, and naming the ground material instead takes the whole ground field including anything enclosed by the object — so the route has to be chosen from what the object actually is, not from what worked on the last file. Check the available presets before assuming a colour is reachable.
trajectory.produces: White-ground plates for the void-bearing objects in which what is see-through in the photograph reads as ground rather than as captured sweep.

trajectory.action: Produce the versions that will sit on the grocer sheet's colour, keeping the whole chain at png so alpha survives, and decide per object which can carry a genuine transparent placement and which must go onto the panel some other way.
trajectory.judgement: The only alpha source in this family is the same knockout that fills enclosed regions, so transparency and open interiors are not both available on the same object. That is a design decision, not a technical shrug: the SKUs that cut cleanly go on the panel as cutouts, and the ones that do not have to be presented so that nothing false is shown. One lossy step anywhere in the chain destroys the alpha for everything downstream and the damage shows up two deliverables later rather than here.
trajectory.produces: A transparent cutout set for the SKUs that support it, a declared treatment for the ones that do not, and the reasoning behind the split.

trajectory.action: Derive the square store primaries from the camera-scale masters, centring the product, and read the tradeoff report on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: Downscale only. The crop tool will quietly enlarge up to a two-times cap and report it only in a field that is easy to skip, so the no-interpolation bar has to be checked per file rather than asserted once.
trajectory.produces: Seven square store primaries named to the SKU list.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark from the burned crate end: select it at ink level by naming the burn's own colour, medium and form rather than the board it sits on, invert, crop to the returned bounds, and trace.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the board and returns a plank-shaped blob that still traces successfully; naming the graphic's own visual properties pulls it to the burn. And the polarity has to be right before tracing or the result is a black box with the letterforms knocked out of it, which also succeeds.
trajectory.produces: A first two-colour vector state of the mark.

trajectory.action: Give the trace the hygiene the tool does not: inject the viewBox it omits and strip the opaque full-canvas rectangle at path index zero. Build the second, full-colour state from a white-knockout plate of the same selection, and keep a high-resolution raster plate of the mark for the surfaces that cannot accept vector.
trajectory.judgement: Placeable and traceable are not the same thing. Without a viewBox the mark will not scale in any layout, and with the background rectangle still attached it puts a white box under itself the moment it lands on the bramble panel. The InDesign template and the reference board will both take a raster and neither will take an SVG, so the plate is not a spare — it is the only form the mark can travel in on two of the surfaces this package touches.
trajectory.produces: Two mark states — a transparent scalable two-colour cut and a full-colour plate — plus a high-resolution raster plate.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's flat shelf-ticket PDF into a working document, export its IDML, and read the real frame inventory: how many text frames there actually are and which copy lines landed in each, how many graphic frames there are and which is the mark and which is the jar photograph, and what the true bounds of each are.
trajectory.judgement: Never promise a field-per-frame map before looking. What the conversion exposes is not under your control, and the ticket's geometry — including how large the mark is actually reproduced — is inherited from the printer rather than chosen.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory for the ticket with real bounds, and the knowledge of which copy lines share a story with which.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping against whatever the conversion actually exposed. Reconstruct each frame's true story text by unzipping the exported IDML and concatenating its content runs, compute every replacement position from that string rather than from the mapping tool's own readout, order rows sharing one story so earlier edits do not move the ground under later ones, and bind the mark plate to its graphic frame as a one-time static image replacement in the template.
trajectory.judgement: A PDF-derived template has no tokens in it, so the workhorse is replacement against real copy at computed positions. The mapping readout is lossy in a way that leaves the string looking well-formed, so a mapping built from it validates cleanly and lands nowhere; only text reconstructed from the document itself gives positions that are actually true. The mark is a fixed element of the card, not a per-row value, so it belongs in the template rather than in the data.
trajectory.produces: A mapping the validator accepts, and a prepared template whose placeholders have not yet been confirmed — the only trustworthy confirmation being to re-export the IDML and grep its stories for every expected field.

trajectory.action: Clean the roster before merging: resolve the duplicate preserve, normalise the headers, rewrite the photo column into the form the merge's image binding actually requires, and rebind its cells to the white-ground primaries produced in step 8, keyed exactly to the names supplied alongside the data.
trajectory.judgement: Six preserves means six tickets. The duplicate row is a client bookkeeping error, and picking which of its two tasting lines is the real one is a judgement about the copy rather than about the data. The image binding has a strict contract on the header form, the cell form and the key form, and a mismatch anywhere in it produces one static picture on every record rather than an error.
trajectory.produces: A six-row merge source bound to the agent's own image filenames, with the image map keyed to match.

trajectory.action: Merge the six records at one record per page and branch the output: a press file for the printer, and per-record single-page files through the route whose record identity is guaranteed.
trajectory.judgement: Do not name per-record files by their position in the returned list — the ordering of that list is not trustworthy for every output type, and the whole deliverable is worthless to a printer if ticket three is the sour cherry.
trajectory.produces: A six-page press file and six identity-guaranteed single-record files.

trajectory.action: Render the client proofs at true print resolution from the merged document and look at all six, at trim.
trajectory.judgement: Resolution asked for at merge time is silently ignored, so the proof has to be rendered from the merged document instead; and a proof is only a proof if every record is looked at rather than the first one that comes back. This is the first and only place in the engagement where the mark is seen at the size a shopper will see it.
trajectory.produces: Six 300 DPI shelf-ticket proofs, inspected at trim.

trajectory.action: Search for the wide table scene of a preserves range, keeping the query short and generic and passing no orientation filter, exclude generative-tech candidates, and license and download the chosen frame at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: The client cannot supply this frame, so it is a sourcing decision rather than a rescue. Choosing it is art direction against the 9-to-16-dollar band — a scrubbed domestic table, not a styled studio still life — and a 240-pixel thumbnail is all there is to choose from.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale wide frame.

trajectory.action: Bring the licensed frame to the warm house look rather than the product-neutral target, and set it beside the six graded masters and the crate hero.
trajectory.judgement: The lifestyle family and the product family are two targets by design, but they will meet on the line sheet and on the store page, so the point at which they are first put next to each other is the point at which the house look is actually decided.
trajectory.produces: The licensed frame graded toward the house look and set adjacent to the six masters and the crate for the first time.

trajectory.action: Assess the client's own market-stall frame as a source for the launch set at the canvases it is actually large enough to serve, and apply the tonal recovery it needs.
trajectory.judgement: Its dimensions rule it out of the wide store-page hero but leave it comfortably above a square or portrait post, so ruling it out on size alone would be lazy — the client offered it and a stall picture is exactly the register the launch set wants. Whether it can carry a canvas is a question about what survived in its brightest areas, and the only way to answer it is to try to bring them back and look at what moved.
trajectory.produces: An evidenced decision about whether the client's own frame can carry any canvas in the launch set, and which canvas.

trajectory.action: Re-aspect the wide hero for the vertical launch canvas by expanding the short axis with a fixed seed, then cropping, and bring the synthesised band into the house neutral before using it.
trajectory.judgement: Expand rather than crop into the scene, because cropping in throws away the range the picture exists to show. The generated edge is new pixels that were never graded, so it has to be brought to the house target afterwards or the seam shows exactly where the eye lands.
trajectory.produces: A vertical hero and a portrait hero from one wide master.

trajectory.action: Run one recommendation pass per typographic role, read the numeric weights out of each family's own style inventory, launder every name into canonical PostScript form, and build a single kit for the whole package.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own art direction because the tool will not pair, and it has to land on plain-spoken and generous rather than on either luxury or supermarket. Weight numbering is family-specific, so the reflexive value ships the wrong cut silently, and one unresolvable name takes the whole kit down with it.
trajectory.produces: A display and text pairing with correct numeric weights, and one embeddable kit.

trajectory.action: Author the whole collateral set as one self-contained document at mixed canvas sizes: the A4 wholesale line sheet with the range as a real table and the mark reversed out of the bramble panel as the first page, the store page with the wide hero, the mark specification page, the square, portrait and vertical launch canvases, and the written handover.
trajectory.judgement: Photographs have to be pulled down and inlined as data rather than referenced by URL, or they arrive as empty grey boxes at full success. The mark goes in as live SVG so it stays editable vector for two people who will be changing things. Anchor everything from the top left with explicit sizes, because right-anchored auto-sized wrappers collapse and throw their contents off the canvas. Put the line sheet first, because only the first page can be seen in a rendition. The handover is where the commission's judgement becomes transferable to two people running a kitchen — which frames were treated differently and why, why there are two graded targets, why this type pairing at this price band, and what the mark needs in order to survive where it is used.
trajectory.produces: One authored source document covering the whole package including its own handover page.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, upload the payload and export it by URL, then verify by parsing what the importer actually produced and by pulling the document's own rendition back to look at it.
trajectory.judgement: Success is not fidelity — every silent drop this importer makes returns success with no warning — so the only honest verification is reading the normalised output and looking at the rendered page. Seven inlined photographs put the payload far past the inline threshold, so it goes up through the asset path and in by URL.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document in the client's Creative Cloud, verified rather than assumed.

trajectory.action: Create the shared reference board and add the finals to it across more than one call, reading a partial success as partial and re-sending only what failed.
trajectory.judgement: The board is a briefing tool for four people, so the selection is editorial: the graded masters, the store primaries, a raster representation of each state of the mark and the licensed frame belong on it, working intermediates do not. Vector is not accepted here and the placement cap is twelve per call, so the mark travels as a picture of itself and the set has to be split deliberately rather than truncated.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable reference board with verified entity ids and no silently dropped items.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the subject knockout holds an edge on these particular photographs. Two of the six sweep frames are pale, near-luminous contents in clear glass sitting at almost exactly the luminance of the grey sweep behind them, and there is no way to predict from looking at the frames — or from any tool documentation — that detection will find no contrast at the glass shoulder. The failure is only legible once the returned cutout is put on the pure white ground and inspected close-up at the shoulder: one comes back with the edge bitten into, the other with a soft grey rim all the way round. Both calls report full success and the alpha looks entirely plausible in a whole-frame preview.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that dodges it and nothing to do right the first time: the knockout has to be run on every frame to produce the deliverable at all, the tool takes only an image and a background colour and exposes no edge, threshold or feathering parameter to set correctly in advance, and the outcome is a property of the contrast between this jar's contents and this sweep. An agent that planned perfectly gets the identical result. (b) Nothing states it. The client reports that the frames disagree with one another but attributes nothing, names no frame and describes a colour symptom rather than an edge one; the deliverables ask for clean white backgrounds; no asset description, no earlier step and no acceptance line names any frame as fragile or names pale-on-grey luminance as an edge risk. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The repair is a different technique entirely — selecting the sweep material by name, inverting it and filling to the ground rather than asking for the subject — which produces a differently-derived cutout, changes those two SKUs' panel versions and their square primaries, and forces a decision about whether the whole set should now be cut the same way for edge consistency.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the failing SKUs by the material-selection route, then decide whether edge consistency across a listing row requires re-cutting the whole set that way rather than shipping a set cut two different ways; regenerate the panel versions and the square primaries for whatever was re-cut, and update the settings log to record that those frames were treated differently and why.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two of the six store listings ship with a visible grey halo and a chewed glass shoulder against a pure white marketplace tile — the single most conspicuous defect in e-commerce product imagery, sitting in a row beside four clean ones — and the same two carry the damage onto the coloured panel of the grocer sheet, where the halo reads as a dirty outline around the jar.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's flat PDF actually becomes once it is converted. The printed ticket looks like five separately labelled copy fields; the conversion exposes nothing of the kind. The placed images split the flow into two text frames and the split falls in a place nobody would predict, so some of the five lines share one continuous story that can only be edited by ordered offset arithmetic while the rest sit alone — the field-per-frame mapping any reasonable person would plan does not exist. In the same reading the two graphic frames turn out to be distinguishable only by their bounds and their link, and the mark's frame is a fraction of the size the printed card suggests: the reproduction size of the recovered mark is geometry inherited from a printer nobody can ask.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Frame granularity is not under the agent's control and is not visible in the PDF, in the client's description, or in any plan made before the conversion runs; there is no ordering that reveals it earlier, because exporting the document structure IS the earliest possible reveal. Nor is there a setting to get right in advance — the conversion takes no granularity option. (b) Nothing states it. The client says they do not have the working file and nobody there knows how it was built, which is exactly the true position; the asset's visible description reports what the printed card looks like, which is precisely what makes the outcome un-guessable; no asset note gives a frame count or a panel dimension and no acceptance line mentions either. (c) It is not a propagation re-run — nothing has been produced yet to re-run. It switches the mapping strategy from one technique to a different one, decides which graphic frame carries a static element and which carries a per-row column, and hands the mark a reproduction size the agent now has to design against rather than choose.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the planned per-field frame map and rebuild it as ordered offset-based replacements inside the shared story with per-frame replacement for the lines that stand alone; assign the two graphic frames by their bounds rather than by their order; and carry the newly-known mark bounds back to the mark work as a constraint on what state of the mark can actually go on a ticket.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The mapping is built against frames that do not exist, so it is dropped at validation or lands on the wrong story, and the merge produces six tickets that are either unchanged from last spring's copy or partially overwritten mid-sentence, with the jar photograph and the mark in each other's frames — a print run of six wrong tickets going to a grocer.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark still holds at the size the printer's own ticket reproduces it. At full canvas the trace is clean and convincing. At the panel's true size, rendered at print resolution and looked at at trim, the bled char that bridged the 'a' bowl and the ampersand's lower eye closes both counters into solid blobs, and the grain hairs the trace picked up out of the oak read as specks of dirt around the mark. This can only be seen on a rendered proof at trim; it is invisible in the artwork at working size and invisible in every tool response along the way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that reveals it earlier, because the reproduction size is not known until the conversion at step 11 and the print resolution is not applied until the proof is rendered. There is nothing to do right the first time either: the tracing tool takes no options at all — no colour count, no path simplification, no threshold — so the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is required cannot be reasoned to in advance, only chosen after seeing which parts of this particular burn fail. (b) Nothing states it. The brief never asks how small the mark can go and never mentions grain or bleed, describing the burn only as the mark being on the crate end; the acceptance bar asks that the mark read as the same mark everywhere it appears, which is a requirement, not a disclosure of what goes wrong or where. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The repair is new raster work producing an additional artwork state — a differently-prepared selection that excludes the bled lower third, or a plate route that keeps the counters open — and a genuine art-direction decision about whether the ticket gets a simplified small-size cut of the mark that is a different drawing from the large one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Go back into the raster preparation of the mark: re-select excluding the grain-bled region or build the plate differently, re-trace, re-hygiene, and produce a small-size state; then decide whether the package ships one mark or an honestly-declared pair of large and small cuts, write that into the usage note, re-bind the plate in the merge template and re-proof.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six shelf tickets go to press with the brand's only mark reduced to two filled-in blobs surrounded by what looks like specks of dirt — on the one deliverable that sits at eye level in a grocer's aisle, for a client whose single greatest anxiety in the brief was that the mark come back as their mark.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each merged record's copy actually survives its frame at true trim. Five of the six preserves sit comfortably. The damson and bay conserve carries a long name with a batch number and the sour cherry carries a nineteen-word tasting line; on a 90 by 55 millimetre ticket those exceed the frames the printer built, and a fixed frame does not spill — it simply stops rendering, so the proof comes back with a tasting line cut off mid-phrase or a name missing its second half, quietly, on two records out of six. Nothing in the merge response, the validation or the on-screen output reports it; the only readout is looking at each rendered record at trim.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering helps: the copy length interacts with a frame size the agent inherited from the printer at step 11, so neither is knowable in advance, and there is no setting to get right the first time — the template's frames are the printer's, not the agent's, and there is no ruler, no pixel readout and no measurement surface anywhere in the connector. An agent who merged in a different order sees the identical result. Reading the roster shows the copy is long; it cannot show whether it fits. (b) Nothing states it. The client hands over the roster as their copy and says nothing about length; the asset note visible to the client describes it as their six preserves with the ticket copy; no acceptance line names which records are long or that any record is at risk. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. Deciding what to do is craft: cut the batch number, subedit the tasting line to a measure that fits, or change how that field is set — each of which changes the client's own words and has to be justified back to them. The re-merge afterwards is the tail of the checkpoint, not the checkpoint.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Subedit the two long records to a measure the inherited frame will hold, or change the field's typographic treatment, record the copy change so the client can approve it, then re-merge and re-proof all six rather than only the two that were altered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two of the six tickets go to press with the preserve name or the tasting line silently truncated — a card in a grocer's aisle that reads 'Damson & Bay Leaf Conserve, Small' and stops — visible to every shopper and to the grocer who agreed to stock the range, in a print run the client pays for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed wide frame actually sits with the graded set. The only thing available at selection time is a 240-pixel search thumbnail, which carries no usable colour information at all — the frame's true illuminant, the tone of its table surface and the colour of the wood in it are visible for the first time after it has been licensed and downloaded at full resolution, and whether it can be brought to the same house look as the six masters is only answerable once the licensed frame and the graded set are actually put next to each other.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that gets colour information out of a 240-pixel thumbnail, and there is no correct choice to make in advance: licensing is the only way to see the frame. Nor is it fixable by grading alone in every case — if the table in the licensed frame is a cool grey-brown and the house look is warm scrubbed pine, correcting it far enough to agree either wrecks the food in it or drags the whole house target off the founders' language. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for one wide picture of the range on a table and says only that they do not have one; nothing in the assets, the deliverables list or the acceptance bar says anything about the frame's colour, and the acceptance line requiring it to sit with the graded set is a requirement rather than a prediction of failure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The likely response is to license a different frame — a second selection made with entirely different criteria now that the agent knows what the thumbnail conceals — or to move the house target and re-grade the lifestyle family, both of which are decisions with consequences rather than repeats.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Either license a second candidate chosen on different criteria and grade that one to the house look, or accept the frame and shift the lifestyle target — which then means re-grading anything else in the lifestyle family and re-checking it against the founders' colour language before it goes onto the store page and the line sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The store page and the wholesale line sheet open with a hero whose table and light plainly belong to a different kitchen than the six jars sitting under it — the exact 'they look wrong next to each other' complaint the client hired this job to fix, reproduced at the top of the two pages a grocer buyer actually reads.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether anything is left in the client's own market-stall frame to recover. It was shot into a low sun behind the stall and the stall front and the top third of every label are clipped to paper white with no information under them at all — but as a thumbnail it reads merely as a bright, cheerful stall picture, exactly the register the launch set wants, and its dimensions are comfortably above a square or portrait canvas. Whether the highlights come back is a property of what the sensor retained, and the only readout is to apply a highlight recovery and see that absolutely nothing moves.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that dodges it. Its pixel dimensions rule it out of the wide store-page hero, but they leave it entirely viable for two of the three launch canvases, so size cannot settle the question and a careful agent must ask it. There is nothing to set correctly in advance either — no parameter makes clipped pixels recoverable, and no tool response distinguishes 'recovered' from 'moved nothing'. An agent that planned perfectly applies the same recovery and gets the same nothing. (b) Nothing states it. The client offers the frame neutrally and says only that they do not have a wide table picture; no asset note mentions the sun or the clipping, no deliverable excludes the frame, and no acceptance line names it. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to re-source that launch canvas from a different upstream artefact entirely — the graded product set, the crate, or the licensed frame re-cropped — which changes what that canvas is a picture of and therefore what the launch set as a whole says about the brand.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Drop the stall frame from the launch set, re-source the affected canvas from another artefact and re-derive it at that canvas's size and ratio, and record in the handover why the client's own picture could not be used so they do not hand it over again next season.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: One of the three launch canvases ships with a blown-out stall picture whose labels have no fronts and whose whole upper half is blank paper white — the range the post exists to sell is illegible in it — sitting beside two immaculately graded canvases in the same set.

deliverables.name: range_masters_v2
deliverables.spec: Eight frames brought to their correct target: the six preserve sweep masters and the gift-crate master corrected individually to one shared product neutral, one white point and one black point, judged with all seven adjacent as they sit in a listing row; plus the licensed wide table frame graded to the warm house look rather than the product neutral, with the two families declared as two deliberate targets. The crate frame levelled. Every frame the client supplied accounted for, with a stated verdict on any frame not carried forward and the evidence behind it. Delivered at camera scale, no frame exceeding its source dimensions.

deliverables.name: store_primaries
deliverables.spec: Seven square store pictures on a pure white ground — six preserves plus the gift crate — product optically centred, nothing touching the edge, no shadow, no invented reflection, downscaled from the camera-scale masters with no interpolated pixels; plus the matching versions for placing on the grocer sheet's coloured panel, each cut so that what is see-through in the photograph is see-through in the file, and with a stated treatment for any SKU the cut cannot serve that way. Named to the SKU list.

deliverables.name: ashgrove_mark_artwork
deliverables.spec: The maker's mark recovered from the burned crate end as usable artwork in more than one state: a transparent, scalable two-colour cut with a real viewBox and no opaque background rectangle attached, a full-colour plate of the same lockup, and a high-resolution raster plate for the surfaces that will not accept vector. The mark reading as the same mark reversed out of the bramble panel as it does on white, and at every size this package reproduces it.

deliverables.name: shelf_tickets_spring
deliverables.spec: Six shelf tickets at 90 by 55 mm, one preserve per page, built from the printer's own 2025 artwork with no working file supplied: a six-page press file in row order, six identity-guaranteed single-record files named to the preserve, and six 300 DPI proofs rendered from the merged document for client sign-off. Exactly one page per preserve, every field on every record live in the merged output, each ticket carrying its own preserve's jar photograph rather than one picture repeated, and every record's full copy present on the rendered proof at trim.

deliverables.name: wholesale_and_launch_collateral
deliverables.spec: One native editable document at mixed canvas sizes that the two founders can change prices in: an A4 wholesale line sheet with the range set as a real editable table, the case terms, and the jars sitting on the bramble panel with the mark reversed out of it; a store page led by the graded wide hero; and a launch set of square, portrait and vertical canvases each consuming a different upstream artefact. Every photograph actually visible in the finished document, the mark present as live vector shapes rather than a raster, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own numeric weight.

deliverables.name: handover_and_reference
deliverables.spec: A written handover page inside the same editable document — the parameters applied to each frame with one line on why that frame differs from its neighbours, the two graded targets and why there are two, any client-supplied frame not used and why, any change made to the client's own ticket copy and the reason, the typefaces chosen and the reasoning for the pairing, and the usage note for the mark including whatever the ticket work established about it — together with a persistent shareable reference board carrying the graded masters, the store primaries, a picture of each state of the mark for briefing, and the licensed wide frame, so the two founders and their two market managers brief from one place. The placeable vector mark itself is delivered in the Express document, since the board takes raster only.

decision_gates: Two targets, not one, and knowing which frame belongs to which: the sweep frames and the crate are a cut-out product family that wants a neutral product target, while the wide table frame is lifestyle and wants the warm house look. Collapsing them into one target either makes the jars look warm and unhygienic in a listing row or makes the table scene look clinical and unappetising, and the error is only obvious where the two families finally meet on the line sheet.

Correcting six frames individually toward one shared neutral rather than applying one batched move, one auto-tone per frame, or two tidy group corrections. Two of the six were shot under a different lamp than the client believes, so any treatment that assumes the batch is homogeneous fractures the row.

Knockout route triage per object rather than per habit: a coherent opaque-contents jar takes the direct route onto white, but an object that encloses a see-through region has to be cut by selecting the ground material, inverting and filling, because the direct route hands that region back filled with whatever the camera captured through it.

Deciding which SKUs can be placed on the grocer sheet's colour at all. The only alpha source in the family is the same knockout that fills enclosed regions, so transparency and open interiors cannot both be had on the same object — which SKUs go on the panel as cutouts, and how the rest are presented instead, is an art-direction call with a technical floor under it.

Naming the mark rather than the board it sits on when selecting the burn. Naming the substrate returns a plank-shaped mask that traces successfully into a rectangle; naming the burn's own colour, medium and letterform returns the ink. And getting the polarity right before tracing, because the wrong polarity also succeeds and returns a black box with the mark knocked out of it.

Vector hygiene as a deliverable requirement rather than an afterthought: a trace with no viewBox will not scale in any layout, and one that still carries its full-canvas background rectangle puts a white box under the mark the instant it lands on the bramble panel. Neither is done for you and neither is reported. And knowing that two of this package's surfaces will not take vector at all, so the mark has to exist as a raster plate as well.

Reading the printer's converted ticket before promising a field map, and computing every replacement position from the document's own reconstructed story text rather than from the mapping tool's readout of it — which is lossy in a way that still validates.

Which graphic frame carries what: the mark is a fixed element of the card and belongs in the template as a one-time static replacement, while the jar photograph is per-record and belongs in the data through the merge's image-column contract. Getting the two the wrong way round produces six identical tickets that all pass.
Resolving the roster's duplicate preserve — and choosing which of its two tasting lines is the real one, which is a copy judgement about the client's own words, not a data-cleaning step.

Choosing the licensed wide frame against the 9-to-16-dollar band from nothing but a 240-pixel thumbnail: a scrubbed domestic table with real food, not a styled studio still life and not a generative-tech candidate.

Expanding the wide frame's short axis rather than cropping into it for the vertical canvas — and then treating the synthesised band as ungraded new pixels that must be brought to the house neutral before use.

The type pairing, which no tool will make: display and text chosen for plain-spoken and generous, weights read from each family's own inventory rather than assumed, and names laundered before the kit is built because one bad name takes the whole kit down.

Getting photographs into the authored collateral as inlined data rather than as URLs, and the mark in as live SVG rather than as a picture — both of which report success either way and only reveal themselves when the finished document is actually looked at. And putting the page that most needs looking at first, because only the first page comes back in a rendition.

Holding the price band across every surface: bramble panel and reversed mark on the grocer sheet is correct, but a near-black ground plus extreme sparseness plus prices pushed out of the reading line is the 48-dollar answer the client ruled out, and a starburst price is the supermarket answer they also ruled out.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these files into a frontier image model and what comes back is unusable on all three of the axes that matter. Identity: these are six real jars with real printed labels, real fill levels and real glass, and a customer who orders from the store page receives exactly the jar in the picture — a regenerated jar invents label copy, changes the fill line and redraws the fruit, which is a returns problem and a labelling problem, not an aesthetic one. The mark is worse: it exists nowhere but as a burn on one crate end, and the entire point of the engagement is that it comes back as the client's mark rather than as a plausible new mark in the same spirit, which is precisely what a generative model produces and precisely what the client said in the brief they do not want. Spec: the deliverables are exact files — seven square store pictures with no interpolated pixels, panel versions whose see-through regions are actually see-through, six shelf tickets at 90 by 55 mm with one page per preserve, each carrying its own preserve's photograph and its own live fields, and 300 DPI proofs at trim. A one-shot render satisfies none of that and cannot even be checked against it. Editability: the client is two people who will be changing prices, so the collateral has to hand over as a native editable document with a real table and live vector, and the tickets have to hand over as a live merge template built from the printer's own artwork so next spring's run is a data change rather than a new commission. A flat picture of a line sheet is not a line sheet. And the whole spine of the job — the recovered mark carried identically from the crate end onto the ticket panel, the store page, the line sheet and the launch set — is a consistency requirement across eleven surfaces that a regenerating model fails by construction, because it draws a slightly different mark every time it draws one.
doability_proof: Every surface and every step is on the verified-live list from CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3.md (audited 2026-09-10, auth account), and nothing banned is required. Imaging: headless upload via asset_initialize_file_upload plus curl PUT plus asset_finalize_file_upload is verified with no file picker; asset_inline_preview returns the pixels so the model can actually look, and close-up edge inspection is reachable by driving image_crop_to_bounds off a returnBbox from an explicit selection and previewing that crop rather than the whole 5472x3648 frame. image_auto_straighten, per-frame image_apply_adjustments, image_apply_auto_tone and the masked adjustment set are verified. image_remove_background with a backgroundColor composites the subject onto a solid ground in one call, and its transparent RGBA output survives both crop tools at png (430x440 RGBA to 430x430 RGBA with 13,371 partial-alpha px preserved). The enclosed-void failure is verified explicitly — a tight crop of a ring badge returned a SOLID OPAQUE DISC, 118,823 opaque px where ~18,000 was correct — and the correct alternative route is verified too: image_select_by_prompt on a named material surface (a 672,398-pixel clean mask of painted wood with the object cut out of it), image_invert_selection, image_fill_area with the verified preset "white" at opacity 100. CRITICALLY, this task does NOT ask for transparency and open interiors on the same object: the fill_area route produces an opaque white-ground plate, and the transparent panel set is restricted to the SKUs that image_remove_background genuinely cuts, with the void-bearing objects given a declared white-tile treatment on the panel instead — the deliverable and the acceptance bar are worded to that split, and no reversed or arbitrary-hex fill is ever required, so image_fill_area is only ever called with a preset confirmed by image_list_presets. image_crop_and_resize's upscale behaviour (2x cap, metadata.upscale_factor, tradeoffs array) is verified, which is what makes the no-interpolation bar checkable rather than asserted; every source is camera-scale (5472x3648 sweeps, 4032x3024 mark, 7360x4912 licensed Stock) so every target downscales, and the 1512x2016 stall frame is above 1080x1080 and 1080x1350 but below a wide hero, which is exactly why its usability is an empirical question rather than an arithmetic one. Mark recovery is verified end to end on exactly this shape of input: ink-level image_select_by_prompt on a printed mark photographed on a surface returned a stroke-only mask with counters excluded (9,372 px for the mark vs 154,926 px when the substrate was named — the documented prompt asymmetry), invert, crop_to_bounds off returnBbox, image_vectorize returned a three-path SVG of a line mark and an 81-path full-colour plate from the fill_area variant; the missing viewBox and the opaque path-zero rectangle are both verified and both must be fixed by hand; image_vectorize takes no options at all, which is what makes raster preparation the only lever. image_generative_expand is live (1024 to 2048 with seeds) and is the sole sanctioned generative call.
